title: Partial indexes and indexes on an expression

videos.script: Lesson 2's workload had a query that counted pending orders, and it was second in the tally. {{tally}} Pending orders are a third of one percent of the table. The server read all two million rows to count them. {{seqscan}} An index on status fixes that. But that index holds an entry for every order ever delivered, and nobody ever asks about those. {{fullindex}} A partial index holds only the rows its own WHERE clause admits. Here, only the pending ones. {{partial}} It answers the same count just as fast, and it is seventy-five times smaller. {{sizes}} The same trick turns a business rule into a constraint: one open cart per customer, enforced by the database. {{carts}} The second half of the lesson goes back to lesson 1. A query wrapped its column in a function, and the index could not help. {{lesson1}} An index can be built on the function itself. On lower of an email, it works at once. {{lower}} On the date of an order, PostgreSQL refuses, with an error that sounds pedantic and is not. {{refuses}} The day an order was placed depends on a time zone. By the end you will know why that stops an index, and how to write the day so it does not. {{title}}
